text: This manual sets out how we work together at the company. It applies to every employee, contractor and temporary worker from their first day. Where a local law gives you stronger protection than this manual, the law wins. Managers may not waive any rule in this manual without written approval from People Operations.
Hiring. This section describes how vacancies are opened, advertised and filled.
Every vacancy must be approved by the department head and by Finance before it is advertised.
Vacancies are advertised internally for at least five working days before external candidates are interviewed.

Interview panels must include at least two people, one of whom has completed the fair hiring course. Panels record a written score for every candidate against the published criteria, and those scores are kept for twelve months.
Offers are made in writing only.
The standard working week is thirty-seven and a half hours, Monday to Friday. Core hours, when everyone is expected to be reachable, are ten in the morning until three in the afternoon.
Outside core hours you may arrange your day as you wish, provided your team knows when you are available and your work is delivered on time.
Overtime requires prior written approval.

Probation. New employees serve a probation period of three months. During probation either side may end the employment with one week of notice. Your manager will meet you at the end of each month to review progress, and will confirm in writing whether probation has been passed, extended once by up to three months, or failed.
Full-time employees receive twenty-five days of paid annual leave per calendar year, in addition to public holidays.
Leave requests are submitted in the leave system at least two weeks in advance for absences longer than three days.
Up to five unused days may be carried over into the next year. Carried-over days expire on the thirty-first of March.
Leave cannot be exchanged for pay, except on termination.
Part-time employees receive leave in proportion to their contracted hours.
If you are too ill to work, tell your manager before your normal start time on the first day of absence.
A medical certificate is required for any illness lasting more than five consecutive working days.
Employees may work remotely for up to three days per week with the agreement of their manager.
Remote work must be carried out from the country named in your employment contract.
Reserved.

Equipment and security. The company provides a laptop, a monitor, a keyboard and a headset for remote work, and these remain company property at all times. You must keep company equipment in a secure place when it is not in use, and you must never leave it unattended in a vehicle, a cafe, a train or any other public place. The laptop must be locked whenever you step away from it, even at home. Only the company virtual private network may be used to reach internal systems; public wireless networks may be used only with the virtual private network switched on. You must install security updates within three days of being prompted, and you must not disable the disk encryption, the firewall or the endpoint protection software. Family members and visitors may not use company equipment for any purpose. Printed documents containing customer or personal data must be shredded and must not be placed in household recycling. If equipment is lost, stolen or damaged you must report it to the service desk within twenty-four hours, and to the police where theft is suspected. When your employment ends, all equipment must be returned within seven days, in the packaging supplied by the company, and the cost of any item that is not returned may be deducted from your final pay where the law allows.
The company pays a fixed monthly allowance towards home internet costs.
You remain responsible for a safe and ergonomic workspace at home and must complete the home workstation self-assessment once a year.
Managers may require attendance in the office for specific meetings with forty-eight hours of notice.
Remote working arrangements are reviewed every six months.
See also Section 8.
Business expenses are reimbursed when they are necessary, reasonable and supported by an itemised receipt.
Claims must be submitted within sixty days of the expense. Late claims are paid only with the approval of the Finance Director.
Travel is booked in economy class for flights shorter than six hours. Rail is preferred over air for journeys under four hours door to door.
Alcohol is not reimbursable.
Personal data about customers and colleagues may be used only for the purpose for which it was collected, and must be stored only in approved systems.
Reserved.
Suspected data breaches must be reported to the security team within one hour of discovery, at any time of day. Do not attempt to investigate or contain a breach yourself.

Disciplinary procedure. Concerns about conduct are first raised informally by your manager. If the concern continues, a formal meeting is held, at which you may be accompanied by a colleague. Possible outcomes are no action, a written warning, a final written warning, or dismissal. You may appeal any formal outcome within ten working days, and the appeal is heard by a manager who was not involved in the original decision.
Working day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
Manager means the person you report to, or someone acting on their behalf.
